**Finding: Compliant (at fallback)** — no redline proposed.

The agreement does impose a Customer-side minimum (the monthly fee floors in § 5(a)), so this is not the preferred "usage only" position. But it clears the fallback on every material term:

| Fallback requirement | Document |
|---|---|
| Commitment limited to current 12-month term | § 13 (p0078): 1-year term, auto-renew in one-year increments, 30-day non-renewal notice |
| Reducible/exitable on 30 days' notice | § 14 (p0079): Client's at-will termination; fees stop the last day of the month following notice |
| True-up rather than penalty | No shortfall, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere; § 2(a) confirms Client is not obligated to use the License |

Since a clause at the fallback is acceptable and not redlined, I left § 5(a) untouched.

Two items I noted in the rationale rather than flagging:
- **§ 14's "Subject to Section 4"** — § 4 is TrueLink's commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than \_\_\_\_ months." That blank could theoretically be filled with a long period and argued to keep the Support Services minimum alive past termination. Worth watching at signature, but as drafted it is a vendor-side obligation running in our favour.
- **§ 6 (p0047)** carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and challenge rights — a billing-transparency issue belonging to the audit/disputes rule.

I also declined to double-flag § 3(i) (p0042), which requires Client to order a credit report per underwriting approval; that is a requirements/exclusivity term, not a minimum-volume commitment with a shortfall consequence.
